messages.text: Request from the operator: could we recommend books to customers from what they've bought before? Investigate first.
Plan: look at how many customers have enough history to recommend from, and what the privacy notice allows.

Only about 6% of customers have more than three online purchases, and the privacy notice doesn't cover profiling. Recommendations would be poor for most people and need a notice change. I recommend not doing it; the staff picks shelf does the job better for now.
Agreed, drop it.
Author names with particles (de, van, von) sort correctly in the purchase history. The existing docs already describe this correctly, so no doc change is needed for this part.

Pulled the constants in the purchase history up to the top of the file so they are easy to find and change. CI on #262 is still running; the browser tests are the slow part as usual. Then the purchase history, and the docs page that describes it.
Not delivered: too little purchase history and the privacy notice doesn't cover it; the operator agreed to drop it.
Request from the operator: the nightly import now takes two hours and overlaps opening. Make it faster.
Plan: profile it first. Likely a query per title and covers downloaded serially; switch to bulk upserts and parallel cover downloads within the distributor's limits.
The new test_import_query_count runs in under a second and the full suite is green locally. Checked the server log from a local run; nothing new appears after the change.
Got the cover download working against the copy of the database from the seed script, including the archived rows. Pushed to PR #264; CI is running. Next I will look at the import loop.

Prices in the import loop come from the shop's own price, not the publisher's recommended price, when the two differ. #264 has the latest commits; the lint job flagged an unused import, which is gone now.
The bulk upsert shows prices with VAT for physical books and the zero rate is applied as before. The existing docs already describe this correctly, so no doc change is needed for this part.
Profile: 4,000 selects and 4,000 updates one by one, and covers downloaded one at a time even when unchanged. Bulk upsert plus skipping unchanged covers: the import now takes six minutes.
Leave the schedule; the distributor publishes at 1am.
Force-pushed #264 after squashing the fixup commits so the history reads cleanly. Ran the whole suite twice to make sure test_import_bulk_upsert does not depend on test order.
Done: PR #264 merged. The nightly import runs in six minutes instead of two hours.

messages.text: Request from the operator: parents ask for books by age. Add age ranges and a children's page that filters by them.
Plan: books carry an age range (from the distributor feed where present, editable by staff); a children's landing page filters by 0-3, 4-7, 8-11 and teen.

I checked the age range field with the seed catalogue's 4,000 titles and the three-volume set that has one ISBN per volume. Ran the whole suite twice to make sure test_age_filter does not depend on test order.
Make the age buttons big and friendly, the page is for parents with kids pulling at them.
